meta.title: ILL Watch — Open-source threat intelligence and SOC platform
meta.description: ILL Watch collects threat intelligence, ranks vulnerabilities by real risk, correlates them with your assets and drives incident response. Open source, self-hosted, on a single server.

announce.text: Pilot programme open to SOC teams, CERTs and MSSPs.

hero.eyebrow: Open-source threat intelligence and SOC platform
hero.lead: ILL Watch collects threat intelligence, ranks vulnerabilities by real risk, correlates them with your assets and drives incident response — on your own server, with no licence fee.

standards.label: Built on the standards your team already uses

features.label: Product
features.title: Everything your SOC does every day, in one place
features.lead: From the first signal to the closed incident, every step lives in the same tool, on the same data.
features.note: Screenshots taken automatically by CI on the fictitious demonstration dataset.
features.prioritize_title: Know which vulnerability to fix first
features.prioritize_text: ILL Watch combines NVD severity, the CISA catalogue of exploited vulnerabilities and the FIRST EPSS probability into one explainable score from 0 to 100.
features.prioritize_b1: Deterministic P0–P3 priority with a remediation deadline
features.prioritize_b2: An actively exploited CVE is never ranked below P1
features.prioritize_b3: Alert as soon as a CVE crosses your threshold
features.triage_text: Every alert arrives with its score broken down. Acknowledge it, or open an incident in one click — nothing is copied by hand.
features.investigate_title: Guided investigation, from first alert to closure
features.investigate_text: Incidents follow the NIST SP 800-61 lifecycle, with an immutable timeline, linked indicators and CVEs, and recommendations for the current phase.
features.investigate_b2: Justified escalation from L1 to L3
features.hunt_text: Submit observables or replay your logs against the database: Tor exit relays, dynamic DNS, algorithmically generated domains, ransomware infrastructure.
features.hunt_b3: Hunts launched straight from an incident
features.correlate_title: Alerts only for what you actually run
features.correlate_text: Your asset inventory is matched against exploited CVEs and indicators, version by version: if your version is not affected, nobody is disturbed.
features.correlate_b1: Product and version matching against the NVD
features.correlate_b2: Your asset addresses checked against indicators
features.measure_text: Time to acknowledge, time to resolve, workload per tier: the figures your management asks for, computed from the timeline.
features.measure_b1: MTTA and MTTR over 7 or 30 days

platform.label: Platform
platform.title: Seven modules. One platform. One audit trail.
platform.lead: The modules share the same data, the same severity scale and the same history — no copying from one tool to another.
platform.feeds_text: CSV, JSON, STIX 2.1, TAXII 2.1, AlienVault OTX, abuse.ch… Indicators normalised, deduplicated, with their provenance and a confidence score.
platform.cve_text: NVD, CISA KEV and FIRST EPSS combined into a deterministic 0–100 score, broken down and explainable. An exploited CVE is never below P1.
platform.corr_text: Asset inventory matched against exploited CVEs and indicators, version by version: an alert is raised only if your version is affected.
platform.soc_text: NIST SP 800-61 lifecycle, immutable timeline, L1 → L3 tiers with justified escalation, MTTA and MTTR measured.
platform.hunt_text: Replay your logs against the whole database: Tor, dynamic DNS, generated domains (DGA), ransomware infrastructure.
platform.intel_text: MITRE ATT&CK techniques and actors, campaigns and attribution by infrastructure, STIX 2.1 sharing and a TAXII 2.1 server.
platform.obs_text: Prometheus metrics, Grafana dashboards, ten operational alerts and backup restores tested every month.

sim.label: Try it
sim.title: See how ILL Watch thinks
sim.lead: The real formula of the ILL Watch engine, running in your browser. Adjust the signals and watch the priority change.
sim.epss_help: Probability of exploitation in the next 30 days
sim.floor: KEV floor: an actively exploited vulnerability is ranked at least P1, whatever its score.
sim.formula: Score = CVSS × 3 + EPSS × 25 + KEV × 25 + exploit × 10 + ransomware × 10, capped at 100. P0 ≥ 80 · P1 ≥ 60 · P2 ≥ 40.
sim.noscript: The simulator needs JavaScript; the formula below still applies.

faq.label: FAQ
faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.free_a: Yes. The source code is public under the MIT licence: you can install, use and modify it with no licence fee. The pilot and support offers are optional services.
faq.data_a: Only on your own server. Geolocation and network enrichment use offline databases; ILL Watch sends no intelligence and no telemetry to any third party.
faq.requirements_q: What do we need to run it?
faq.requirements_a: A Linux server with Docker. The application runs in under {memory} MB of memory; PostgreSQL and Redis are part of the Docker Compose stack.
faq.languages_a: The interface and this site are available in English, French, German, Spanish and Simplified Chinese, chosen automatically from your country and browser. Each user can switch at any time.
faq.ready_a: ILL Watch is in pre-production: the modules are delivered and tested on every change, and the production-hardening milestone is in progress. A guided pilot is the recommended way to start.
faq.integrate_q: Does it work with our existing tools?
faq.integrate_a: Yes, through open standards: STIX 2.1 import and export, a TAXII 2.1 server, a REST API, webhooks for alerts and Prometheus metrics.

platformPage.title: From raw signal to closed incident, in one platform
platformPage.lead: ILL Watch brings together threat intelligence, vulnerability prioritisation, detection, hunting and incident response. Every module works on the same data, under the same audit trail.
platformPage.flow_lead: Each signal follows the same path: no copy-paste between tools, and every decision can be traced back to its source.
platformPage.s1_text: Public and private feeds collected at their own pace, with automatic back-off when a source fails.
platformPage.s2_text: Indicators normalised and deduplicated; each one keeps all of its sources.
platformPage.s3_text: Country and autonomous system offline, confidence computed from source reliability.
platformPage.s4_text: Indicators, CVEs and your assets crossed version by version.
platformPage.s5_text: Deterministic P0–P3 score, explained, with an alert above your threshold.
platformPage.s6_text: Incident opened in one click, escalated, investigated, closed — all traced.
platformPage.feeds_b1: Nine reference sources preconfigured, more in a few clicks
platformPage.feeds_b2: Health of each source and history of every collection run
platformPage.feeds_b3: API keys read from the environment, never stored in the database
platformPage.cve_b1: NVD, CISA KEV and FIRST EPSS synchronised automatically
platformPage.cve_b2: Score broken down signal by signal, with priority history
platformPage.cve_b3: Remediation deadline per priority, alert by webhook
platformPage.corr_b1: Inventory of your products, versions, platforms and addresses
platformPage.corr_b2: Vulnerable version ranges read from the NVD
platformPage.corr_b3: False positives qualified and never reopened
platformPage.soc_b1: Guided NIST SP 800-61 phases and immutable timeline
platformPage.soc_b2: Response recommendations computed from the incident's IOCs and CVEs
platformPage.soc_b3: L1 → L3 tiers, assignment and justified escalation
platformPage.hunt_b1: Six versioned rules, mapped to MITRE ATT&CK where relevant
platformPage.hunt_b2: Hunts launched on demand, on a schedule or from an incident
platformPage.hunt_b3: Matches filtered by rule and severity
platformPage.intel_b1: Campaigns linking an adversary to the IOCs of its infrastructure
platformPage.intel_b2: MITRE ATT&CK actors and techniques imported offline
platformPage.intel_b3: STIX 2.1 export and a read-only TAXII 2.1 server
platformPage.obs_b1: MTTA and MTTR per tier, over 7 or 30 days
platformPage.obs_b2: Prometheus metrics and ready-made Grafana dashboards
platformPage.obs_b3: Ten operational alerts and monthly tested restores

explorer.title: See which techniques ILL Watch helps you detect
explorer.lead: An extract of MITRE ATT&CK covered by the detection rules. Select a technique to see how the platform responds.
explorer.note: ATT&CK® © The MITRE Corporation, reproduced with permission. Extract limited to the techniques mapped to the rules of the current version.
explorer.T1190: A vulnerability in an exposed product is exploited. ILL Watch alerts when an actively exploited CVE, or one with a public exploit, affects a product of your inventory in a vulnerable version — and hunting flags exploited CVEs on your assets.
explorer.T1566_001: Booby-trapped attachments sent by email. When a campaign uses this technique (QakBot for example), ILL Watch links the actor to the IOCs of its infrastructure, so an alert on one of these IOCs carries the right context.
explorer.T1090_003: Traffic relayed through several proxies, such as Tor, to hide its origin. The hunting rule recognises Tor exit relays from the official list.
explorer.T1568: Infrastructure that changes address through dynamic DNS. The hunting rule recognises some forty free dynamic DNS providers favoured by C2 servers and phishing.
explorer.T1568_002: Domain names generated by an algorithm (DGA) to reach command servers. The rule measures how unlikely a name is in English, calibrated on 100,000 real domains.
explorer.T1486: Data encrypted to extort a ransom. The rule flags addresses linked to ransomware infrastructure, and response recommendations ask to isolate hosts and check offline backups.

taxii.title: Share your intelligence in the standard format
taxii.lead: ILL Watch serves its indicators and campaigns over TAXII 2.1, in STIX 2.1, to your SIEM, your firewall or a partner CERT.
taxii.discovery_text: The client finds the TAXII server and its API root. Authentication with an ILL Watch account or an API token.
taxii.collections_text: Two read-only collections: active indicators, and campaigns with their actors and infrastructure.
taxii.objects_text: Indicators added since a given date, paginated, with confidence and severity: ready for a SIEM or a blocklist.
taxii.note: Real requests against the ILL Watch TAXII server; responses abridged, on the fictitious demonstration dataset.

securityPage.title: Security built in, from the first line of code
securityPage.lead: ILL Watch handles sensitive information. It runs on your infrastructure, keeps your data with you, and every security measure can be checked in the source code.
securityPage.arch_lead: No external service is needed to operate. Only the intelligence sources you enable are contacted, over HTTPS.
securityPage.arch_users_text: HTTPS only, through the reverse proxy
securityPage.arch_sources_text: Outbound HTTPS requests only, to the feeds you choose
securityPage.arch_proxy_text: Automatic TLS, security headers, the only exposed port
securityPage.arch_app_text: Authentication, roles, strict content security policy
securityPage.arch_db_text: Not exposed, protected by password, dedicated application role
securityPage.arch_caption: Enrichment (country, autonomous system) uses a local database: no address is sent to a third party.
securityPage.controls_lead: Each of these measures is implemented, tested in CI and documented in the architecture decision records.
securityPage.identity_b2: 15-minute access tokens, rotating refresh tokens with reuse detection
securityPage.identity_b4: Login throttling per account and per address
securityPage.data_b2: Incident timeline and audit log append-only, enforced by the database
securityPage.data_b3: Application database role without structural rights
securityPage.data_b4: Feed API keys read from the environment, never stored
securityPage.app_b1: Strict content security policy and security headers (HSTS, nosniff, frame denial)
securityPage.app_b2: API documentation hidden in production, wildcard CORS refused
securityPage.app_b3: Size and format limits on every collected feed
securityPage.app_b4: Every sensitive action recorded in the audit log, with request identifier
securityPage.supply_b1: All dependencies pinned and audited on every change
securityPage.supply_b2: Code, image and Git history scanned for vulnerabilities and secrets
securityPage.supply_b3: More than 500 tests against a real PostgreSQL database
securityPage.ops_b1: Prometheus metrics and ten operational alerts
securityPage.ops_b2: Backups with restores tested every month
securityPage.ops_b3: Complete instance rebuilt and validated every week
securityPage.ops_b4: Readiness and liveness probes for supervision
securityPage.disclosure_text: Tell us privately before publishing anything. The security policy explains how to report it and what we commit to in return.

aboutPage.title: Making threat intelligence accessible to every defender
aboutPage.lead: ILL Watch is developed by CYBERILL, an initiative that builds open, verifiable cybersecurity tools for organisations of every size, everywhere in the world.
aboutPage.story_p1: Commercial threat intelligence platforms cost tens of thousands per year. Complete open-source alternatives require heavy infrastructure and a team to run them. Between the two, many SOCs, CERTs and public bodies work with spreadsheets and copy-paste.
aboutPage.story_p2: ILL Watch was born in 2026 to close that gap: one platform, on one server, that does the repetitive work of a SOC and leaves the decisions to analysts.
aboutPage.story_p3: The project is open source and driven by measured milestones: a milestone is closed when its criteria are verified on real data, not when the code is merged.
aboutPage.founder_role: Founder and lead developer — IT security specialist (SOC, SIEM, network security, forensics)
aboutPage.measured_text: Every figure we publish is dated, sourced and reproducible.
aboutPage.open_text: The code is public under the MIT licence: anyone can audit it.
aboutPage.sovereign_text: Self-hosted, with no third-party service and no telemetry.
aboutPage.global_text: Five languages, international standards, a light footprint.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.lead: This site collects as little data as possible: no cookies, no tracking, no third-party resources.
privacy.controller_text: The controller within the meaning of the GDPR is {operator}, reachable at {email}. Full details are in the legal notice.
privacy.visit_text: To deliver the pages, the hosting server ({hosting}) processes technical data such as your IP address, the date and the page requested (Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR, legitimate interest in a secure, working site). These logs are kept only as long as the host needs them for security.
privacy.language_text: On your first visit, the site may ask our server for the language of your country. Your IP address is used once, in memory, to find the country in a local database: it is neither stored nor passed on, and the answer contains only the language.
privacy.storage_text: If you choose a language, it is remembered in your browser's local storage so that the site opens in that language next time. Nothing else is stored, and no cookie is set. You can delete it at any time in your browser settings.
privacy.demo_text: If you send a request, we process the details you enter (name, work email, organisation, and optionally job title, country and message) to answer it (Art. 6 (1) (b) and (a) GDPR). Your IP address is not stored with the request. The data is kept for at most 12 months, then deleted. You can withdraw your consent at any time.
privacy.nocookies_text: This site uses no cookies, no audience measurement, no social network plugins and loads no fonts or scripts from third parties.
privacy.rights_text: You have the right of access, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing, data portability and objection, and the right to withdraw consent. Write to {email}. You may also lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority.
privacy.changes_text: We update this policy when the site changes. The current version always applies.
